rule.title: AWS ECS Task Definition That Queries The Credential Endpoint
rule.author: Darin Smith

es.summary: Un principal de AWS registró, consultó o ejecutó una task definition de ECS cuyo comando de contenedor hace referencia a $AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI, la variable que apunta a las credenciales del rol de la tarea. Puede indicar un backdoor que roba las credenciales del task role.
es.what_it_detects: Eventos de CloudTrail con eventSource ecs.amazonaws.com y eventName DescribeTaskDefinition, RegisterTaskDefinition o RunTask, cuyo campo requestParameters.containerDefinitions.command contiene $AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI.
es.why_it_matters: Un atacante puede agregar a una task definition un comando que consulte el endpoint de credenciales (169.254.170.2) y las envíe fuera, como hace el módulo ecs__backdoor_task_def de Pacu. Así obtiene persistencia y los privilegios del task role (ATT&CK T1525, Implant Internal Image).
triage_steps: Identifique al actor: userIdentity.arn, tipo de identidad, sourceIPAddress y userAgent. Compruebe si es un pipeline de CI/CD o un usuario esperado.
Lea el comando completo en requestParameters.containerDefinitions.command. Busque curl/wget, destinos externos, codificación base64 o envío de la respuesta a otro host.
Compare la nueva revisión con la anterior de la misma family (DescribeTaskDefinition) para ver qué cambió, incluidos image, taskRoleArn y variables de entorno.
Determine los permisos del taskRoleArn asociado y qué recursos podría alcanzar un atacante con esas credenciales.
Busque en CloudTrail eventos del mismo actor en +/- 15 minutos: ListTaskDefinitions, DescribeTaskDefinition, UpdateService, RunTask, iam:PassRole.
Verifique si alguna sesión del task role se usó desde sourceIPAddress ajenas a su cuenta o VPC después del evento.
Revise alertas previas para el mismo principal, la misma IP de origen y el mismo cluster o family.
false_positives: Task definitions modificadas por razones válidas para solicitar credenciales al Task Metadata Service, por ejemplo scripts de arranque que usan el rol de la tarea.
Imágenes o scripts de diagnóstico de equipos de plataforma que validan la configuración del task role.
Pruebas autorizadas de pentest o red team con herramientas como Pacu.
response_steps: Confirme con el dueño del servicio o del pipeline si el cambio estaba aprobado antes de actuar.
Si no es legítimo, actualice los servicios a una revisión conocida como buena, detenga las tareas afectadas y desregistre la revisión maliciosa.
Revoque las sesiones activas del task role (política de denegación con aws:TokenIssueTime) y desactive o rote las credenciales del principal que hizo el cambio.
Bloquee los destinos externos identificados y revise el uso de las credenciales robadas en CloudTrail.
Restrinja ecs:RegisterTaskDefinition e iam:PassRole al mínimo necesario y documente el incidente.
es.severity_rationale: Medium porque existen usos legítimos del endpoint de credenciales, pero un comando inesperado puede exponer las credenciales del task role y dar persistencia.

en.summary: An AWS principal registered, described or ran an ECS task definition whose container command references $AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI, the variable that points to the task role credentials. This may be a backdoor that steals task role credentials.
en.what_it_detects: CloudTrail events with eventSource ecs.amazonaws.com and eventName DescribeTaskDefinition, RegisterTaskDefinition or RunTask where requestParameters.containerDefinitions.command contains $AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI.
en.why_it_matters: An attacker can add a command to a task definition that queries the credential endpoint (169.254.170.2) and sends the result out, as Pacu's ecs__backdoor_task_def module does. That gives persistence and the task role's privileges (ATT&CK T1525, Implant Internal Image).
triage_steps: Identify the actor: userIdentity.arn, identity type, sourceIPAddress and userAgent. Check whether it is an expected CI/CD pipeline or user.
Read the full requestParameters.containerDefinitions.command. Look for curl/wget, external destinations, base64 encoding or the response being sent to another host.
Compare the new revision with the previous revision of the same family (DescribeTaskDefinition), including image, taskRoleArn and environment variables.
Find out what the taskRoleArn can do and which resources an attacker could reach with those credentials.
Search CloudTrail for the same actor within +/- 15 minutes: ListTaskDefinitions, DescribeTaskDefinition, UpdateService, RunTask, iam:PassRole.
Check whether task role sessions were used after the event from a sourceIPAddress outside your accounts or VPCs.
Review earlier alerts for the same principal, source IP, cluster or task family.
false_positives: Task definitions changed for valid reasons to request credentials from the Task Metadata Service, such as startup scripts that use the task role.
Diagnostic images or scripts from platform teams that check the task role configuration.
Authorized pentest or red team exercises using tools such as Pacu.
response_steps: Confirm with the service or pipeline owner whether the change was approved before taking action.
If not legitimate, roll services back to a known-good revision, stop affected tasks and deregister the malicious revision.
Revoke active task role sessions (deny policy with aws:TokenIssueTime) and disable or rotate credentials of the principal that made the change.
Block identified external destinations and trace any use of the stolen credentials in CloudTrail.
Limit ecs:RegisterTaskDefinition and iam:PassRole to least privilege and document the incident.
en.severity_rationale: Medium because legitimate uses of the credential endpoint exist, but an unexpected command can expose task role credentials and provide persistence.

positive.description: RegisterTaskDefinition with a container command that queries the credential endpoint and posts it to an external host
RunTask overriding the command to read task role credentials

negative.description: Legitimate RegisterTaskDefinition that only queries the task metadata endpoint, not the credential endpoint
Credential URI string in a command but from a non-ECS event source
